name: GridMotion-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The tilted grid fills the frame with photos and word tiles all readable and evenly spread.

tagline: A tilted wall of photos slides sideways as the pointer crosses.
summary: Four rows of photo and text tiles sit in a grid turned about fifteen degrees off level. Moving the pointer left or right shoves alternating rows in opposite directions with a soft lag.
appearance: A dark backdrop holds a large four-by-seven grid of rounded square tiles, tilted counter-clockwise so its rows run diagonally. Most tiles are cropped photographs in muted tones; every fourth one is a black tile with a single white word.
behaviour: Rows glide horizontally in alternating directions, drifting further the further the pointer sits from the middle, each row lagging a little differently. The grid is oversized, so its edges always run past the frame.
demo_content: Camera bodies, forest windows, laptops, snowy peaks and black word tiles reading Depth, Flow and similar labels.
search_phrases: tilted photo wall that slides on mouse
image wall for a portfolio landing
grid of photos with drift effect
use_when: A landing or portfolio section needs a wall of imagery that comes alive with the pointer.
avoid_when: You need tiles that stay still or legible on touch: rows only respond to a mouse and are always cropped at the edges.
customise: Pass up to 28 items as strings, image URLs or nodes, plus the radial gradient colour. Row count, tilt, gap and slide range are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Twenty-eight tiles move with GSAP each tick, with no canvas or 3D scene.

a11y.note: Photos are CSS backgrounds with no alt text, and there is no reduced-motion path for the row drift.

polish_why: Well paced drift and a coherent tilt; outer tiles are always half cut off.
title: Grid Motion
